research_decision_or_candidate: Use 28 October 1835 as the declaration date; 34 northern rangatira signed at Waitangi.
evidence_basis: NZ History; Te Ara; Archives NZ item IA9-1
implementation_boundary: Do not convert the declaration date into a single-person accession date.

research_decision_or_candidate: Represent authority as collective among the participating chiefs/rangatira, not a monarchy or centralized presidential office.
evidence_basis: He Whakaputanga articles 1–3; Waitangi Tribunal Stage 1
implementation_boundary: No individual HOS succession array should be generated from signatory names.

research_decision_or_candidate: Do not treat the 34 initial northern signatories as all iwi/hapū or all Māori authority; 18 additional signatures were added by 1839.
evidence_basis: NZ History signatory database; Te Ara
implementation_boundary: No full-island sovereignty/control claim from the signatory count alone.

research_decision_or_candidate: Record the annual congress as a constitutional intention; evidence states that the planned congress did not come to pass.
evidence_basis: Te Ara, Original Declaration; He Whakaputanga overview
implementation_boundary: Do not implement an operating parliament/event loop from the plan alone.

research_decision_or_candidate: James Busby is an external British Resident and convenor/administrator, not a Māori HOS or elected executive of the United Tribes.
implementation_boundary: Do not insert Busby as an MAO leader or succession record.

research_decision_or_candidate: Treat 6 February 1840 as a major treaty/authority transition, not automatic proof that every Māori polity dissolved or that all rangatira ceded sovereignty.
evidence_basis: Waitangi Tribunal, Te Paparahi o Te Raki Stage 1
implementation_boundary: Existing registry hist_to requires owner/reviewer-approved temporal interpretation before any data patch.

research_decision_or_candidate: Preserve the distinction between te Tiriti Māori text, English text, and the Waitangi Tribunal Stage 1 finding limited to its inquiry/signatories.
evidence_basis: Waitangi Tribunal Stage 1; Te Ara comparison of texts
implementation_boundary: No universal legal conclusion beyond the cited inquiry scope.

research_decision_or_candidate: Keep MLY as a gameplay aggregate only; label it explicitly as a modelling container, not a historically unified sovereign polity.
evidence_basis: Official Conference of Rulers; current registry note
implementation_boundary: No common national ruler, flag-state succession, or unified 1836 cabinet should be inferred.

research_decision_or_candidate: 1836 Perak ruler candidate: Sultan Shahabuddin Riayat Shah (1830–1851).
evidence_basis: Perak Sultanate official list; official coronation volume
implementation_boundary: State-local candidate only; retain local source provenance and exact dates as supported by official chronology.

research_decision_or_candidate: 1836 Selangor ruler candidate: Sultan Muhammad Shah (1826–1857); district chiefs retained substantial practical autonomy.
implementation_boundary: Do not equate nominal Sultanate with centralized control of every district.

research_decision_or_candidate: Model Sultan and Temenggong as distinct offices. Temenggong Daeng Ibrahim held the Temenggong office from 1825; British recognition is dated 1839 and transfer of Johor government to him was by treaty in 1855.
implementation_boundary: Do not backdate the 1855 transfer or collapse Temenggong and Sultan into one ruler.

research_decision_or_candidate: Bendahara Tun Ali (appointed 1806; rule commonly dated 1806–1857) is a local Bendahara authority, not a single Sultan of all MLY.
evidence_basis: W. Linehan, A History of Pahang (1936)
implementation_boundary: Treat term/date as year-level secondary evidence; further primary corroboration is requested.

research_decision_or_candidate: Represent the Luak and Undang/customary authorities alongside any Yamtuan Besar; do not reduce the polity to a uniform hereditary monarchy without further source checking.
evidence_basis: Buyong Adil, Sejarah Negeri Sembilan; specialist thesis on Yamtuan structure
implementation_boundary: Exact 1836 succession/authority relationships remain open; no named candidate patch yet.

research_decision_or_candidate: Kedah was invaded/occupied by Siam in 1821 and Ahmad Tajuddin was restored in 1842; Perlis was reorganized as a Siamese administrative unit in 1839 and Syed Hussein was formally installed as Raja in 1843.
evidence_basis: Oxford academic article; official Perlis royal genealogy
implementation_boundary: These are not simple members of the five-polity MLY aggregate; do not silently backdate a separate sovereign Perlis in 1836.

research_decision_or_candidate: Retain the conflict around Sultan Muhammad I's death (1835/1837) and Long Zainal/Long Senik power transition; Sultan Muhammad II is dated from 1838, not 1836.
evidence_basis: Kelantan Museum; peer-reviewed chronology discussion; academic Hikayat Seri Kelantan study
implementation_boundary: Do not insert Muhammad II as a 1836 ruler or choose a disputed succession without review.

research_decision_or_candidate: For 1836, distinguish Sultan Muhammad I's formal reign (1836–1839 in the UniSZA lineage) from Tengku Omar's rival/previous claim and exile; Omar returns in 1839.
implementation_boundary: No single uncontested succession transition should be inferred from a simplified head-of-state field.

research_decision_or_candidate: Treat Siamese suzerainty/tributary relationships as differentiated political relationships with local rulers, not automatic direct control or annexation.
evidence_basis: Tsinghua field archive study; Siam Society historical study; state-specific histories
implementation_boundary: Requires explicit relationship semantics and per-polity sources before game-data implementation.

research_decision_or_candidate: Do not backdate the Federated Malay States to 1836. They formed in 1895/1896 and comprised Perak, Selangor, Negeri Sembilan and Pahang; Johor and northern states remained outside.
implementation_boundary: No 1836 federation flag, shared government or succession chain.

research_decision_or_candidate: A single 1836–1936 succession array for MLY is structurally invalid because its constituent states follow different protectorate, federation and colonial trajectories.
evidence_basis: Official Conference of Rulers; Johor, Perak and other state histories
implementation_boundary: Treat MLY as a region/grouping/container until component polity modelling is approved.
